notes:
BOTH RED BEATS STAYED RED, and both are correct - Jesus in the flesh, and a
red-letter KJV inks both.
  j1  John 8:12  'I am the light of the world...'
  j2  John 9:5   'As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.'
(j2 is John 9:5, not John 8 - the verse reference is recorded on the segment so
nobody has to guess later. Same book, same speaker, still red.)

FRAMING SPLIT ADDED. John 8:12 in the KJV opens 'Then spake Jesus again unto them,
saying, I am the light of the world...' The first clause is John writing, not
Jesus speaking, and a red-letter Bible leaves it black. It is now its own segment:
  s12  John 8:12  'Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying,'  SCRIPTURE, blue.
s12 and j1 sit on the SAME still (ST2), consecutive beats over one image, so the
artwork and the edit the viewer sees are unchanged.

LIFTED - THE BLIND MAN'S OWN LINE. n3 said 'He opened blind eyes and proved it,'
which is the narrator reporting the best sentence in John 9 instead of letting the
man say it. Added verbatim:
  s25  John 9:25  'One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.'
SCRIPTURE, blue - he is a man in the story, not Deity. n3 was rewritten to retell
him, on the same still.

ADDED RETELLING: j2 had no retelling after it, so n2b is new.

WOMEN - CONSIDERED AND LEFT OUT, ON PURPOSE. John 8:12 comes immediately after the
woman taken in adultery, who says 'No man, Lord' (John 8:11). It is a real woman's
line and it is verbatim available. It was left out because pulling that scene in
would change what this video is about - it is a sixty-second 'I am' declaration,
and the stills (a blind man's closed eyes, eyes opening) carry the John 9 thread,
not the John 8 courtyard. Flagging it here because it is the right woman's line for
a DIFFERENT build, and it should get one.

WHY-LAW: he did not describe light and walk away. He put his hands on a man born
blind. Milk framing - the claim is checkable, and the man it happened to could only
say one thing about it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus stood among the temple courts and spoke into the noise of the crowd.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying,

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Not a lamp that burns out. A light that walks with you, so you're never feeling your way blind.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Later, as He met a man born blind, He said it again.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While I am here in the world, He said, I am the light of it. Then He knelt down in the dirt in front of a man who had never seen anything, and went to work.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One thing I know, the man told them afterward — I was blind, and now I see. He didn't just describe light. He opened blind eyes and proved it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Stop groping in the dark. Walk with the Light.

stills_wanted.ST2: ST2 now carries John's framing line AND the declaration itself. Frame the declaration: Jesus in the temple court at the hour the great lamps are lit, standing still while the crowd moves around him, light falling on him rather than from him. Certain, unraised voice, not performing.
stills_wanted.ST5: ST5 now carries the healed man's verbatim testimony and its retelling. Frame him AFTER, under questioning: a plain man standing in front of seated officials, eyes wide open and steady, shrugging slightly - out-argued on every point and completely unmoved, because he is the evidence. Not the miracle; the aftermath.
stills_wanted.ST6: ST6 now carries John 9:5 and its retelling. Frame the moment before the healing: Jesus crouched low in the dust, hands working, the blind man's face turned toward a voice he cannot see. Tender and certain at once - the light doing something with its hands.
